t: #3529 Count Cells in Overlapping Horizontal and Vertical Substrings
o: Flatten the grid in row-major order to get the horizontal string H (wrapping across rows, no wrap at the very end) and in column-major order to get the vertical string V. Find every start index where pattern occurs in H (these cover horizontal runs of cells) and in V (vertical runs). A cell counts iff it lies in at least one horizontal match AND at least one vertical match. With m·n ≤ 10⁵, string matching in O(mn) plus range-marking with difference arrays is the way. Example 2: "aba" matches horizontally and vertically, overlapping on 4 cells.
k: Row-major flattening encodes all horizontal wrapped substrings; column-major encodes vertical ones.
A horizontal match at flat index i covers flat cells i..i+L-1; a vertical match at column-major index i covers column-major cells i..i+L-1.
Mark covered cells with difference arrays, then intersect the two coverings per cell.

a.i: Hash both flattened strings and slide a window of length |pattern|; equal hashes indicate a match. Difference arrays turn each match into two point updates, and one prefix pass reveals covered cells.
s: Compute pattern hash; find all matching start indices in H and V via rolling hash.
Diff-mark covered ranges; prefix-sum to get boolean coverage for horizontal (flat index) and vertical (column-major index).
Count cells t where horizontal-covered(t) and vertical-covered(colMajorIndex(t)).

c.python:
class Solution:
    def countCells(self, grid: List[List[str]], pattern: str) -> int:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        H = ''.join(''.join(r) for r in grid)
        V = ''.join(grid[i][j] for j in range(n) for i in range(m))
        L = len(pattern); MOD = (1 << 61) - 1; B = 131
        ph = 0
        for c in pattern: ph = (ph * B + ord(c)) % MOD
        def starts(s):
            ln = len(s); h = [0] * (ln + 1); p = [1] * (ln + 1)
            for i, c in enumerate(s):
                h[i + 1] = (h[i] * B + ord(c)) % MOD
                p[i + 1] = p[i] * B % MOD
            pw = pow(B, L, MOD); res = []
            for i in range(ln - L + 1):
                if (h[i + L] - h[i] * pw) % MOD == ph: res.append(i)
            return res
        mn = m * n
        rh, ch = [0] * (mn + 1), [0] * (mn + 1)
        for i in starts(H): rh[i] += 1; rh[i + L] -= 1
        for i in starts(V): ch[i] += 1; ch[i + L] -= 1
        hc, vc = [False] * mn, [False] * mn
        a = 0
        for t in range(mn): a += rh[t]; hc[t] = a > 0
        a = 0
        for t in range(mn): a += ch[t]; vc[t] = a > 0
        return sum(1 for t in range(mn) if hc[t] and vc[(t % n) * m + t // n])

a.t: O(mn) — building strings, hashing, and marking are all linear in the flattened size.
a.sp: O(mn) — flattened strings, hash arrays, and coverage arrays.

a.i: Same framework, but find occurrences with the Knuth–Morris–Pratt automaton, which guarantees linear time with zero collision risk.
s: Build the KMP failure table of the pattern.
Run KMP over H and V collecting match start indices.
Diff-mark ranges, prefix-sum into coverage booleans, and count intersecting cells.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def countCells(self, grid: List[List[str]], pattern: str) -> int:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        H = ''.join(''.join(r) for r in grid)
        V = ''.join(grid[i][j] for j in range(n) for i in range(m))
        L = len(pattern)
        fail = [0] * L; k = 0
        for i in range(1, L):
            while k and pattern[i] != pattern[k]: k = fail[k - 1]
            if pattern[i] == pattern[k]: k += 1
            fail[i] = k
        def occ(s):
            res = []; k = 0
            for i, c in enumerate(s):
                while k and c != pattern[k]: k = fail[k - 1]
                if c == pattern[k]: k += 1
                if k == L: res.append(i - L + 1); k = fail[k - 1]
            return res
        mn = m * n
        rh, ch = [0] * (mn + 1), [0] * (mn + 1)
        for i in occ(H): rh[i] += 1; rh[i + L] -= 1
        for i in occ(V): ch[i] += 1; ch[i + L] -= 1
        hc, vc = [False] * mn, [False] * mn
        a = 0
        for t in range(mn): a += rh[t]; hc[t] = a > 0
        a = 0
        for t in range(mn): a += ch[t]; vc[t] = a > 0
        return sum(1 for t in range(mn) if hc[t] and vc[(t % n) * m + t // n])

a.t: O(mn) — KMP is linear in text length for each direction.
a.sp: O(mn) — flattened strings, failure table, coverage arrays.

w: Either approach passes; rolling hash is faster to write, KMP avoids hash-collision worries. Key pitfalls: getting the coordinate mapping right (column-major index t ↔ cell (t mod m, t div m), flat index t ↔ (t div n, t mod n)); marking coverage with difference arrays instead of per-match loops (which can be quadratic when the pattern is tiny and matches are many). Follow-up: count cells covered by matches in at least k of several directions.
